japanese: すみません、駅はどこですか？
reading: すみません、えきはどこですか？
romaji: sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka?
english: Excuse me, where is the station?
literalMeaning: Excuse me, where is the station?
naturalUsage: A simple, natural way to ask for the nearest station.

japanese: この電車は東京駅に行きますか？
reading: このでんしゃはとうきょうえきにいきますか？
romaji: kono densha wa Toukyou-eki ni ikimasu ka?
english: Does this train go to Tokyo Station?
literalMeaning: Does this train go to Tokyo Station?
naturalUsage: Use before boarding when you want to confirm the destination.

japanese: これは新宿行きですか？
reading: これはしんじゅくいきですか？
literalMeaning: Is this Shinjuku-bound?
naturalUsage: 〜行き is the standard way to say a train is bound for a destination.

japanese: 何番線ですか？
reading: なんばんせんですか？
literalMeaning: What platform number is it?
naturalUsage: A concise question commonly used with station staff.

japanese: この電車で合っていますか？
reading: このでんしゃであっていますか？
english: Am I on the right train?
literalMeaning: Is this train correct?
naturalUsage: Natural when you want reassurance before or after boarding.

japanese: 次の電車は何時ですか？
reading: つぎのでんしゃはなんじですか？
romaji: tsugi no densha wa nanji desu ka?
english: What time is the next train?
literalMeaning: What time is the next train?
naturalUsage: Useful after missing a train or while waiting.

japanese: 出口はどちらですか？
reading: でぐちはどちらですか？
literalMeaning: Which direction is the exit?
naturalUsage: Polite and natural at stations.

japanese: 改札はどこですか？
reading: かいさつはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where are the ticket gates?
naturalUsage: Useful in large stations where gates can be hard to find.

japanese: すみません、通ります。
reading: すみません、とおります。
literalMeaning: Excuse me, I will pass through.
naturalUsage: Natural when moving through a crowded train or platform.

japanese: 次で降ります。
reading: つぎでおります。
english: I'm getting off at the next stop.
literalMeaning: I get off at the next one.
naturalUsage: Useful when moving toward the door before your stop.

japanese: この席、空いていますか？
reading: このせき、あいていますか？
literalMeaning: Is this seat open?
naturalUsage: Use before sitting when it is unclear whether someone is using the seat.

japanese: 荷物をここに置いてもいいですか？
reading: にもつをここにおいてもいいですか？
romaji: nimotsu o koko ni oite mo ii desu ka?
english: May I put my luggage here?
literalMeaning: Is it okay if I put my luggage here?
naturalUsage: Useful around luggage racks or shared storage areas.

japanese: この電車は快速ですか？
reading: このでんしゃはかいそくですか？
romaji: kono densha wa kaisoku desu ka?
literalMeaning: Is this train rapid?
naturalUsage: Use to confirm the service type before boarding.

japanese: この電車は各駅停車ですか？
reading: このでんしゃはかくえきていしゃですか？
romaji: kono densha wa kakueki-teisha desu ka?
english: Is this a local train that stops at every station?
literalMeaning: Does this train stop at every station?
naturalUsage: Useful when distinguishing local service from rapid or express trains.

japanese: 駅員さんに聞いてみます。
reading: えきいんさんにきいてみます。
english: I'll ask a station staff member.
literalMeaning: I'll try asking station staff.
naturalUsage: Useful when deciding to ask for help.

japanese: 切符を一枚お願いします。
reading: きっぷをいちまいおねがいします。
literalMeaning: One ticket, please.
naturalUsage: Basic ticket-purchase phrase at a staffed counter.

japanese: 新宿までの切符をお願いします。
reading: しんじゅくまでのきっぷをおねがいします。
romaji: Shinjuku made no kippu o onegai shimasu.
literalMeaning: A ticket as far as Shinjuku, please.
naturalUsage: Natural way to specify your destination when buying a ticket.

japanese: 往復でお願いします。
reading: おうふくでおねがいします。
literalMeaning: As a round trip, please.
naturalUsage: Useful where round-trip tickets are available.

japanese: 片道でお願いします。
reading: かたみちでおねがいします。
literalMeaning: As a one-way trip, please.
naturalUsage: Useful when clarifying that you need a one-way ticket.

japanese: 指定席をお願いします。
reading: していせきをおねがいします。
literalMeaning: A reserved seat, please.
naturalUsage: Common at JR counters and for limited express or Shinkansen travel.

japanese: 自由席はありますか？
reading: じゆうせきはありますか？
literalMeaning: Are there unreserved seats?
naturalUsage: Useful when checking whether a service offers unreserved seating.

japanese: 窓側の席はありますか？
reading: まどがわのせきはありますか？
romaji: madogawa no seki wa arimasu ka?
literalMeaning: Is there a seat on the window side?
naturalUsage: Useful when requesting a reserved seat.

japanese: 通路側の席はありますか？
reading: つうろがわのせきはありますか？
romaji: tsuurogawa no seki wa arimasu ka?
literalMeaning: Is there a seat on the aisle side?
naturalUsage: Useful when requesting an aisle seat.

japanese: ICカードは使えますか？
reading: あいしーかーどはつかえますか？
english: Can I use an IC card?
literalMeaning: Can an IC card be used?
naturalUsage: Useful for checking Suica/PASMO/ICOCA compatibility.

japanese: この切符で乗れますか？
reading: このきっぷでのれますか？
english: Can I ride with this ticket?
literalMeaning: Can I board using this ticket?
naturalUsage: Useful when unsure whether your ticket covers the service.

japanese: 特急券は必要ですか？
reading: とっきゅうけんはひつようですか？
english: Do I need a limited express ticket?
literalMeaning: Is a limited express ticket necessary?
naturalUsage: Some trains require an additional limited-express ticket.

japanese: 乗車券だけで大丈夫ですか？
reading: じょうしゃけんだけでだいじょうぶですか？
romaji: joushaken dake de daijoubu desu ka?
english: Is the basic fare ticket enough?
literalMeaning: Is just the boarding ticket okay?
naturalUsage: Use when checking whether another surcharge ticket is required.

japanese: 切符をなくしました。
reading: きっぷをなくしました。
literalMeaning: I lost the ticket.
naturalUsage: Tell station staff immediately if you lose a paper ticket.

japanese: 切符が改札を通りません。
reading: きっぷがかいさつをとおりません。
english: My ticket won't go through the gate.
literalMeaning: The ticket does not pass through the gate.
naturalUsage: Use when an automatic gate rejects your ticket.

japanese: 精算はどこでできますか？
reading: せいさんはどこでできますか？
romaji: seisan wa doko de dekimasu ka?
english: Where can I adjust the fare?
literalMeaning: Where can I settle the fare difference?
naturalUsage: Useful when your ticket or IC-card fare needs adjustment.

japanese: 新宿行きは何番線ですか？
reading: しんじゅくいきはなんばんせんですか？
english: Which platform is the train for Shinjuku?
literalMeaning: What platform number is the Shinjuku-bound train?
naturalUsage: One of the most useful station questions.

japanese: このホームで合っていますか？
reading: このほーむであっていますか？
literalMeaning: Is this platform correct?
naturalUsage: Natural way to confirm you are waiting in the right place.

japanese: 電車はどちらから来ますか？
reading: でんしゃはどちらからきますか？
romaji: densha wa dochira kara kimasu ka?
english: Which direction will the train come from?
literalMeaning: From which direction does the train come?
naturalUsage: Useful at unfamiliar platforms.

japanese: 何両目ですか？
reading: なんりょうめですか？
literalMeaning: Which numbered train car is it?
naturalUsage: Useful when looking for a reserved car or meeting point.

japanese: 指定席は何号車ですか？
reading: していせきはなんごうしゃですか？
english: Which car has the reserved seats?
literalMeaning: What car number is the reserved-seat car?
naturalUsage: Useful on limited express and Shinkansen services.

japanese: 自由席は何号車ですか？
reading: じゆうせきはなんごうしゃですか？
literalMeaning: What car number has unreserved seats?
naturalUsage: Useful for trains with both reserved and non-reserved cars.

japanese: 女性専用車はどこですか？
reading: じょせいせんようしゃはどこですか？
romaji: josei senyou-sha wa doko desu ka?
literalMeaning: Where is the women-only train car?
naturalUsage: Useful on lines that operate women-only cars during certain hours.

japanese: エレベーターはどこですか？
reading: えれべーたーはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the elevator?
naturalUsage: Useful with luggage, strollers, or mobility needs.

japanese: エスカレーターはどこですか？
reading: えすかれーたーはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the escalator?
naturalUsage: Useful in large multi-level stations.

japanese: 階段はどこですか？
reading: かいだんはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where are the stairs?
naturalUsage: Simple navigation question inside stations.

japanese: ホームはこの先ですか？
reading: ほーむはこのさきですか？
romaji: hoomu wa kono saki desu ka?
literalMeaning: Is the platform beyond here?
naturalUsage: Useful when following signs in a large station.

japanese: この電車は何分後に来ますか？
reading: このでんしゃはなんぷんごにきますか？
romaji: kono densha wa nan-pun go ni kimasu ka?
english: How many minutes until this train arrives?
literalMeaning: After how many minutes does this train come?
naturalUsage: Useful when departure information is unclear.

japanese: この電車はここに止まりますか？
reading: このでんしゃはここにとまりますか？
romaji: kono densha wa koko ni tomarimasu ka?
literalMeaning: Does this train stop here?
naturalUsage: Use to confirm whether a service calls at a station.

japanese: 並ぶ場所はここですか？
reading: ならぶばしょはここですか？
romaji: narabu basho wa koko desu ka?
english: Is this where I should line up?
literalMeaning: Is the place to line up here?
naturalUsage: Useful where platform markings indicate different services.

japanese: この列で合っていますか？
reading: このれつであっていますか？
english: Is this the right line to queue in?
literalMeaning: Is this queue correct?
naturalUsage: Useful on busy platforms with multiple boarding lines.

japanese: どこで乗り換えますか？
reading: どこでのりかえますか？
literalMeaning: Where do I change trains?
naturalUsage: Core phrase for navigating multi-line journeys.

japanese: 新宿で乗り換えですか？
reading: しんじゅくでのりかえですか？
literalMeaning: Is the transfer at Shinjuku?
naturalUsage: Use to confirm the transfer station.

japanese: 乗り換えは何番線ですか？
reading: のりかえはなんばんせんですか？
english: Which platform do I transfer to?
literalMeaning: What platform number is the transfer?
naturalUsage: Useful when a transfer requires changing platforms.

japanese: 乗り換え時間はどのくらいですか？
reading: のりかえじかんはどのくらいですか？
romaji: norikae jikan wa dono kurai desu ka?
english: How long does the transfer take?
literalMeaning: About how much time is the transfer?
naturalUsage: Useful in large stations or with tight connections.

japanese: この乗り換えで間に合いますか？
reading: こののりかえでまにあいますか？
literalMeaning: Will I make it with this transfer?
naturalUsage: Natural when you are worried about a short connection.

japanese: 乗り換え口はどこですか？
reading: のりかえぐちはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the transfer entrance/gate?
naturalUsage: Useful in stations with dedicated transfer gates.

japanese: 一度改札を出ますか？
reading: いちどかいさつをでますか？
english: Do I need to exit the gates once?
literalMeaning: Do I leave the ticket gates once?
naturalUsage: Useful when transferring between different operators.

japanese: このまま乗っていて大丈夫ですか？
reading: このままのっていてだいじょうぶですか？
romaji: kono mama notte ite daijoubu desu ka?
english: Can I stay on this train?
literalMeaning: Is it okay to remain riding like this?
naturalUsage: Useful for through-services where the train continues onto another line.

japanese: この電車は途中で行き先が変わりますか？
reading: このでんしゃはとちゅうでいきさきがかわりますか？
romaji: kono densha wa tochuu de ikisaki ga kawarimasu ka?
english: Does this train's destination change on the way?
literalMeaning: Does this train's destination change midway?
naturalUsage: Useful for services that split, terminate, or change designation.

japanese: 直通ですか？
reading: ちょくつうですか？
literalMeaning: Is it direct/through-running?
naturalUsage: Short and useful when checking whether you can stay on the same train.

japanese: 乗り換えなしで行けますか？
reading: のりかえなしでいけますか？
english: Can I get there without transferring?
literalMeaning: Can I go without a transfer?
naturalUsage: Useful when looking for the simplest route.

japanese: 次の駅で乗り換えですか？
reading: つぎのえきでのりかえですか？
romaji: tsugi no eki de norikae desu ka?
english: Do I transfer at the next station?
literalMeaning: Is the transfer at the next station?
naturalUsage: Useful when checking transfer timing.

japanese: 乗り換え案内を見せてもらえますか？
reading: のりかえあんないをみせてもらえますか？
romaji: norikae annai o misete moraemasu ka?
english: Could you show me the transfer information?
literalMeaning: Could I have you show me the transfer guidance?
naturalUsage: Useful when asking staff to point out a route on a map or screen.

japanese: この線からJRに乗り換えたいです。
reading: このせんからじぇいあーるにのりかえたいです。
romaji: kono sen kara jei-aaru ni norikaetai desu.
english: I'd like to transfer from this line to JR.
literalMeaning: I want to transfer from this line to JR.
naturalUsage: Useful when switching between railway operators.

japanese: 地下鉄への乗り換えはどこですか？
reading: ちかてつへののりかえはどこですか？
romaji: chikatetsu e no norikae wa doko desu ka?
english: Where is the transfer to the subway?
literalMeaning: Where is the transfer toward the subway?
naturalUsage: Useful in major stations connecting railways and subway lines.

japanese: 東口はどこですか？
reading: ひがしぐちはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the East Exit?
naturalUsage: Replace 東口 with other named exits as needed.

japanese: 西口はどこですか？
reading: にしぐちはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the West Exit?
naturalUsage: Very useful in stations with several named exits.

japanese: 南口はどこですか？
reading: みなみぐちはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the South Exit?
naturalUsage: Useful when meeting someone or following map directions.

japanese: 北口はどこですか？
reading: きたぐちはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the North Exit?
naturalUsage: Useful in larger station complexes.

japanese: A3出口はどこですか？
reading: えーさんでぐちはどこですか？
romaji: ee-san deguchi wa doko desu ka?
literalMeaning: Where is A3 Exit?
naturalUsage: Especially useful in subway stations with numbered or lettered exits.

japanese: この出口で合っていますか？
reading: このでぐちであっていますか？
literalMeaning: Is this exit correct?
naturalUsage: Use before leaving a large station where the wrong exit may add a long walk.

japanese: 駅の地図はありますか？
reading: えきのちずはありますか？
romaji: eki no chizu wa arimasu ka?
literalMeaning: Is there a map of the station?
naturalUsage: Useful at information counters or in complex stations.

japanese: 出口までどのくらいかかりますか？
reading: でぐちまでどのくらいかかりますか？
romaji: deguchi made dono kurai kakarimasu ka?
english: How long does it take to get to the exit?
literalMeaning: About how long does it take as far as the exit?
naturalUsage: Useful in very large stations.

japanese: この道で合っていますか？
reading: このみちであっていますか？
english: Am I going the right way?
literalMeaning: Is this route correct?
naturalUsage: Natural general-purpose confirmation phrase.

japanese: まっすぐですか？
reading: まっすぐですか？
literalMeaning: Is it straight?
naturalUsage: Short follow-up when someone gives directions.

japanese: 右ですか、左ですか？
reading: みぎですか、ひだりですか？
romaji: migi desu ka, hidari desu ka?
literalMeaning: Is it right, or left?
naturalUsage: Useful clarification when directions are unclear.

japanese: この階で合っていますか？
reading: このかいであっていますか？
literalMeaning: Is this floor correct?
naturalUsage: Useful in multi-level station buildings.

japanese: 案内所はどこですか？
reading: あんないじょはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the information counter?
naturalUsage: Useful when you need more detailed help.

japanese: コインロッカーはどこですか？
reading: こいんろっかーはどこですか？
romaji: koin rokkaa wa doko desu ka?
literalMeaning: Where are the coin lockers?
naturalUsage: Extremely useful for travelers carrying luggage.

japanese: トイレはどこですか？
reading: といれはどこですか？
literalMeaning: Where is the toilet?
naturalUsage: Simple and essential station phrase.

japanese: 電車を間違えました。
reading: でんしゃをまちがえました。
english: I got on the wrong train.
literalMeaning: I made a mistake with the train.
naturalUsage: Tell staff when you realize you took the wrong service.

japanese: 乗り過ごしました。
reading: のりすごしました。
literalMeaning: I rode past my stop.
naturalUsage: Natural phrase when you accidentally stay on too long.

japanese: 乗り換えに間に合いませんでした。
reading: のりかえにまにあいませんでした。
literalMeaning: I did not make it in time for the transfer.
naturalUsage: Useful when asking staff what to do next.

japanese: 電車が遅れていますか？
reading: でんしゃがおくれていますか？
literalMeaning: Is the train running late?
naturalUsage: Useful when the departure board or announcements are unclear.

japanese: どのくらい遅れていますか？
reading: どのくらいおくれていますか？
literalMeaning: About how late is it?
naturalUsage: Natural follow-up when a delay has been announced.

japanese: 運転見合わせですか？
reading: うんてんみあわせですか？
literalMeaning: Is train operation temporarily suspended?
naturalUsage: 運転見合わせ is a common railway disruption term in Japan.

japanese: 振替輸送はありますか？
reading: ふりかえゆそうはありますか？
literalMeaning: Is substitute transportation available?
naturalUsage: Useful during major disruptions when another route may accept affected passengers.

japanese: 別の行き方はありますか？
reading: べつのいきかたはありますか？
romaji: betsu no ikikata wa arimasu ka?
english: Is there another way to get there?
literalMeaning: Is there another way of going?
naturalUsage: Very useful during delays, closures, or missed connections.

japanese: ICカードが反応しません。
reading: あいしーかーどがはんのうしません。
literalMeaning: The IC card is not responding.
naturalUsage: Use at a ticket gate when your IC card cannot be read.

japanese: 改札から出られません。
reading: かいさつからでられません。
english: I can't get out through the ticket gate.
literalMeaning: I cannot exit from the ticket gate.
naturalUsage: Useful when your fare or IC card needs adjustment.

japanese: 荷物を電車に忘れました。
reading: にもつをでんしゃにわすれました。
english: I left my luggage on the train.
literalMeaning: I forgot my luggage on the train.
naturalUsage: Tell station staff as soon as possible and give train/time details.

japanese: 落とし物はどこで聞けばいいですか？
reading: おとしものはどこできけばいいですか？
romaji: otoshimono wa doko de kikeba ii desu ka?
english: Where should I ask about a lost item?
literalMeaning: Where would it be good to ask about lost property?
naturalUsage: Natural way to ask where the lost-and-found desk or office is.

japanese: 終電を逃しました。
reading: しゅうでんをのがしました。
literalMeaning: I missed the final train.
naturalUsage: Useful when asking staff about alternative transportation after the last service.

japanese: 終電はもう終わりましたか？
reading: しゅうでんはもうおわりましたか？
english: Has the last train already gone?
literalMeaning: Has the final train already finished?
naturalUsage: Useful late at night when checking whether service has ended.

japanese: 電車の中に忘れ物をしたかもしれません。
reading: でんしゃのなかにわすれものをしたかもしれません。
romaji: densha no naka ni wasuremono o shita kamo shiremasen.
english: I may have left something on the train.
literalMeaning: I might have forgotten something inside the train.
naturalUsage: A softer way to explain that you are not completely sure where an item was lost.
